comparisons.peer_topic: Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) Requirements and Compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation must maintain a minimum SLR of 3.0% plus a 2.0% leverage buffer to avoid restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments, with the numerator defined as quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital and the denominator based on total leverage exposure. At December 31, 2024, its insured depository institution subsidiaries exceeded the 6.0% minimum SLR required to be considered well capitalized under the PCA framework.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures detail leverage ratio requirements for banking entities. GS specifies that its leverage ratio calculation includes profits subject to audit and approval (contributing 54 basis points), while BAC defines its Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) mechanics, including the numerator (Basel 3 Tier 1 capital) and denominator (total leverage exposure), and notes compliance with minimum SLR requirements to avoid distribution restrictions. Both address the composition and regulatory minimums of leverage ratios, though GS focuses on a specific accounting adjustment within the ratio and BAC focuses on the structural definition and buffer requirements.

sentences.text: In the table above, the leverage ratio as of December 2024 reflected profits that are still subject to annual audit by GSBE's external auditors and approval by GSBE's shareholder (GS Bank USA) for inclusion in risk-based capital.
These profits contributed 54 basis points to the leverage ratio as of December 2024.

The Corporation is also required to maintain a minimum supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) of 3.0 percent plus a leverage buffer of 2.0 percent in order to avoid certain restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to executive officers.
The numerator of the SLR is quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital.

The denominator is total leverage exposure based on the daily average of the sum of on-balance sheet exposures less permitted deductions and the simple average of certain off-balance sheet exposures, as of the end of each month in a quarter.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's Supplementary Leverage Ratio was 5.8% as of December 31, 2024, largely unchanged from the prior year, as higher Tier 1 Capital was offset by an increase in Total Leverage Exposure.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures report on the Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) for the fiscal year 2024. C explicitly states its SLR was 5.8% as of December 31, 2024, driven by Tier 1 Capital and Total Leverage Exposure. While GS does not report a specific SLR percentage in the selected sentences, it discusses the calculation of its leverage ratio and the inclusion of profits, which is a component of the leverage ratio framework relevant to SLR calculations. Both concern the quantitative status and components of leverage ratios.
